title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, a representative validator-trace excerpt, quantitative analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models promises productivity gains but raises safety and correctness concerns when model outputs trigger network changes. A common operational pattern to mitigate such risks is generate–verify–repair (GVR): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator checks correctness and policy constraints, and when necessary a repair module synthesizes corrected candidates or escalates to human review. Prior architectural work motivates GVR adoption in NetOps, yet systematic, preregistered measurement of validator coverage (false-positive and false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive value for guarded end-to-end success is lacking.

We preregistered study AC-2026-03 to measure the incremental value of validator-triggered repair in an interpretable, controlled way. The design is paired and uses shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task a single initial generator output is produced and reused by both conditions (baseline: accept the candidate as-is; guarded: permit validator-triggered repair). Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise downstream from deterministic validation and repair, isolating the validator/repair pathway from sampling variability. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered test is an exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and closed-loop verifier architectures have been proposed and evaluated in code and systems domains to reduce stochastic generator error and enable deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Recent NetOps and AIOps benchmark efforts document substantive failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate insertion of verifier layers [2],[3]. Prototype reports and system proposals advocate self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. Survey work in telecommunications and NetOps emphasizes adaptation and verification trade-offs and motivates evaluation of verification cost versus nominal correctness [5].

These prior records motivate a measurement focus on validator soundness and operational impact but do not deliver a standardized, empirically estimable validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows. Our study was designed and preregistered to begin filling that measurement gap under strict preregistration and artifact-archiving practices; we treat prior demonstrations as architectural motivation rather than as empirical evidence that validators already achieve comprehensive coverage for operational NetOps.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and overall design. The study preregistration (AC-2026-03) specified adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini (provider bundle 'openai_responses'); task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar two-sided test and paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistration included power calculations targeting detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power and deterministic contamination/exclusion rules (duplicate SHA-256 and semantic-similarity embedding cosine > 0.95).

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty levels labeled 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, a compact natural-language intent, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. These structured constraints produce intent→configuration mappings that a deterministic validator can mechanically check. The execution bundle records task_manifest.jsonl and representative task entries; analysis/contamination_summary.csv shows no contamination exclusions in this run.

Model and sampling configuration. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Important artifact-grounded note: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling variability may still exist and is accounted for in the execution manifest audit.

Validator and scoring. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator performs mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts when generated. The preregistered binary success label uses validator.valid under the scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call per failed candidate; repairs would toggle repair_applied and be recorded in repair_provider_trace fields.

Execution controls and missingness. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). The primary analysis used complete-pair analysis only; sensitivity analyses were preregistered to treat missing/incomplete episodes as failures. The execution manifest shows completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200. Deterministic provider-call auditing recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with one shared initial generation per task and with shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200. No contamination exclusions occurred (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. All numeric analysis files are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and match these reported values.

Representative validator-trace excerpt. To illustrate validator semantics and why no repairs were triggered, we reproduce a compact, verbatim excerpt from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (pair-000004):

pair_id: pair-000004
normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
parsed_command_count: 4
required_command_count: 4
observed_touched_field_count: 3
valid: true
repair_applied: false
validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
validator_version: 5.0

For this exemplar the parsed and required command counts matched, no violation codes were emitted, and the validator did not request repair. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode.

Exploratory diagnostics. Because repair_applied = false for all episodes, per-validator FP/FN estimates and repair-latency distributions are degenerate in this execution. The archived raw responses (execution/raw_results.jsonl) and full validator traces permit reanalysis under alternative scoring or under follow-up fault-injection arms. We report two compact artifact-grounded summaries as tables below that are drawn directly from archived CSV artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the degenerate outcome. The preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates downstream validator-triggered repair effects: the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical initial candidate per pair, so any paired difference could only arise from deterministic validation/repair. The observed ceiling (baseline = guarded = 1.0) therefore indicates that, for the selected synthetic task bank, declared model seeds, and validator implementation, there were zero mechanically detectable defects for the validator to reject or to repair. This artifact-grounded result invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) because with baseline success = 1.0 the paired estimator has zero variance and no statistical test can detect an improvement that cannot occur in the observed data.

Root causes visible in the artifacts. Three archived, mutually reinforcing determinants explain the degenerate outcome: (1) task-generator constraints and chosen generation seeds produced candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic checks for the recorded samples; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime removed generator variability as a source of candidate invalidity; (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but, by design, cannot detect certain semantic intent misalignments that are correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent.

Prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments. To produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility, the archived infrastructure supports direct, preregisterable next steps that we recommend and that are implementable without manual artifact fabrication:
  1) Fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically inject controlled faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). This will create measurable baseline invalidity and allow the guarded condition to demonstrate repair benefit.
  2) Multi-sample stochastic generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task, with independent sampling seeds recorded. Allow guarded pipelines to accept any validator-approved draw or to request repair; generator variability will create opportunities for validator rejections and repairs.
  3) Multi-validator and model diversity: add alternative validator implementations and at least one additional model family to quantify sensitivity to validator design and model selection.
Each prescription is supported by the archived adapter semantics and task-generation mechanics; implementing them would produce non-degenerate data suitable for estimating FP/FN, detection latency, repair utility, and predictive R^2 against an operational-impact proxy as originally planned.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate downstream effects but introduce single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but may not capture semantic intent alignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model execution (gpt-5-mini), and single deterministic validator limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance in the primary estimand; inferential conclusions about validator benefit are not possible from this execution alone. These limitations are documented in the archived artifacts and motivate the artifact-grounded follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, sampled gpt-5-mini outputs, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions were therefore invalidated by this ceiling outcome. We publish the execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and offer concrete, artifact-grounded, preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
